source.author: verg
source.text: Tum pater omnipotens, aliquem indignatus ab umbris mortalem infernis ad lumina surgere vitae, ipse repertorem medicinae talis et artis fulmine Phoebigenam Stygias detrusit ad undas.
source.text_original: Tum pater omnipotens, aliquem indignatus ab umbris / mortalem infernis ad lumina surgere vitae, / ipse repertorem medicinae talis et artis / fulmine Phoebigenam Stygias detrusit ad undas.
source.text_english: Then the almighty Father, indignant that a mortal should rise from the shadows below to the lights of life, himself, the discoverer of such healing and of such an art, hurled Phoebigena with his thunderbolt down to the Stygian waters.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: clamat summus poeta eos omnes qui muentas uitam excoluere per artes aput inferos esse ipsumque illum repertorem medicinae talis et artis ad Stygias undas fulmine detrusum, ut intellegamus quantum ualeat pater omnipotens, qui etiam deos fulminibus exstinguat.
reuse.text_original: clamat summus poeta eos omnes qui muentas uitam excoluere per artes aput inferos esse ipsumque illum repertorem medicinae talis et artis ad Stygias undas fulmine detrusum, ut intellegamus quantum ualeat pater omnipotens, qui etiam deos fulminibus exstinguat.
reuse.text_english: The greatest poet proclaims that all those who cultivated life by way of the silent arts are among the dead below, and that even the discoverer himself of such medicine and of that art was hurled by a thunderbolt to the Stygian waters, so that we may understand how great is the power of the almighty Father, who even extinguishes the gods with thunderbolts.
